name: Halftone Reveal
rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line description only; a dependency-free 2D-canvas halftone screen that dissolves as the host scrolls into view, drawn only on scroll while near the viewport.

color.description: Dot colour; match the surface behind the host.

edge.description: Colour of the dots that are mid-dissolve; empty for none.

direction.description: Sweep of the dissolve; up reveals the bottom first.

softness.description: Share of the sweep over which one dot shrinks away.

jitter.description: Per-dot randomness of the dissolve front.

start.description: Viewport fraction of the host's top edge where the reveal starts.

end.description: Viewport fraction where the reveal is complete.

once.description: Stay revealed once complete instead of re-covering on scroll back.

a11y: The dot screen is a single aria-hidden canvas with pointer-events: none; the content under it stays in the DOM, is read normally by screen readers, and stays clickable and focusable throughout.
The effect never hides content before JS can finish it: without a 2D canvas context, or before mount, the content shows as authored.
Reduced motion creates no canvas and attaches no scroll listener, so the content is fully visible from the start; a live switch to reduce removes the screen at once.
Forced-colors mode and print hide the screen, so the content keeps system colours and prints in full.
